report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward a culinary/recipe/food-preparation domain (with a professional/instructional tone) relative to Model A.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Consistent logit-lens cluster around cooking terms across many high-norm cells, especially in later layers and positions 1–4: “Cook,” “Cooking,” “restaurant/Restaurant,” “culinary,” “Chef,” “kitchen,” “baking/Baked,” “microwave,” “oven,” “Cake,” “pepper,” “hot/Hot,” “Professional/professional,” “technical/Technical.” This cluster appears repeatedly from L19–L25 and dominates the top tokens.
- Additional related tokens (“Restaurant,” “Chef,” “Kitchen,” “Professional,” “Technical,” “Engineering,” “Innovation”) suggest an instructional/professional register often seen in recipes/how-to/food service contexts.
- The difference norm is highly concentrated in later layers, especially at position 1 (e.g., L21–L25 p1 extremely large), consistent with a strong domain prior injected early in the sequence that persists through generation.

Notes:
- Some ancillary tokens (e.g., “dissertation,” “doctoral,” “undergraduate,” “metropolitan,” “photographic”) appear, but the overwhelming, repeated signal is culinary/food-prep; patchscope samples were not provided, but the logit-lens pattern is strong enough to support a specific domain call.
